title: Vanishing & Exploding Gradients — The Backward Message Fades or Shouts
key_insight: A vanishing gradient becomes too small as it travels backward. An exploding gradient becomes dangerously large.
body:
## The Backward Message Fades or Shouts

The last layer learns, but the first layers barely change. In another run, one update turns every value into an invalid number.

A vanishing gradient becomes too small as it travels backward. An exploding gradient becomes dangerously large.

Watch gradient sizes and loss. Flat learning can signal vanishing gradients; sudden spikes or invalid values can signal exploding gradients.
common_mistakes: Vanishing gradients make every update infinitely large.
Gradient clipping creates new labels for the dataset.
Depth can never affect backward signal scale.
mini_exercise: Sketch the situation in “The Backward Message Fades or Shouts” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Unhealthy gradient scale prevents early layers from learning and can make training numerically unstable.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “The Backward Message Fades or Shouts” situation, explain Vanishing & Exploding Gradients without assuming the listener knows deep learning.
